Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

limit noun and verb

also limits, set a limit, there’s a limit, within limits, speed limit, limited, restrict, limitation, limitations, constraint, constraints

classical

Hor. S. 1.1.106: est modus in rēbus
Plaut. Poen. 238: modus omnibus rēbus … optimus est habitū
Traupman 218, 383: vēlōcitātis modus, speed limit

modus, modī m.

noun, second declension

measure, limit (how far, how much)

To set a limit: modum facere with the genitive (inimīcitiārum modum facere, Cic. Sull. 48, Lewis & Short) or modum statuere with the dative (cupidinibus statuat nātūra modum, Hor. S. 1.2.111); without limit, sine modō.

Other words

  • fīnis, fīnis m. — a boundary, a limit; (plural) territory

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.1.106: sunt certī dēnique fīnēs

    Also the end of something (see end).

  • terminus, terminī m. — a boundary stone, a bound

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.70: nūllīs ut terminīs circumscrībat aut dēfīniat jūs suum (Lewis & Short)

  • terminō, termināre, termināvī, terminātum — limit, bound

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.62: paucīs litterārum notīs termināvit

  • circumscrībō, circumscrībere, circumscrīpsī, circumscrīptum — restrict, hem in

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Mil. 88: senātus, crēdō, praetōrem eum circumscrīpsisset

Examples

  • est modus in rēbus, sunt certī dēnique fīnēs

    there is a measure in things; there are, in short, fixed limitsHor. S. 1.1.106

  • modus omnibus rēbus, soror, optimus est habitū

    keeping within limits, sister, is best in everythingPlaut. Poen. 238

  • quī sonōs vōcis, quī īnfīnītī vidēbantur, paucīs litterārum notīs termināvit

    the man who confined the sounds of the voice, which seemed limitless, to a few lettersCic. Tusc. 1.62

  • vēlōcitātis modus

    the speed limitTraupman 383

See also end, border, edge, enough.
